title: Chicken Thigh Stretch Dinner
seoTitle: Chicken Thigh Stretch Dinner | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Roasted thighs, beans, and vegetables that go farther
subtitle: Roasted thighs, beans, and vegetables that go farther
description: Spiced chicken thighs roast over potatoes, peppers, and beans for a complete economical pan dinner.

steps.title: Heat oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F and line sheet pans with parchment or foil.

steps.title: Season chicken
steps.instruction: Rub thighs with oil, paprika, garlic, salt, and pepper, then wash hands thoroughly.

steps.title: Cut potatoes
steps.instruction: Cut potatoes into equal 1-inch pieces so they finish at the same time.

steps.title: Dry chickpeas
steps.instruction: Drain and pat chickpeas dry; wet chickpeas steam instead of browning.

steps.title: Arrange pans
steps.instruction: Spread potatoes, peppers, onion, and chickpeas in single layers, leaving space between pieces.

steps.title: Add chicken
steps.instruction: Place thighs skin-side up among the vegetables without crowding or overlapping them.

steps.title: Roast
steps.instruction: Roast, rotating pans halfway, until vegetables brown and the thickest thigh reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Crisp skin
steps.instruction: Broil for 2 minutes only if skin needs crisping; watch closely because paprika can burn.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Cover loosely and keep chicken above 140°F while portions are arranged.

steps.title: Serve pans
steps.instruction: Give each person a thigh with roasted potatoes, chickpeas, peppers, and pan juices.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Chicken thighs — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Chicken thighs and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use two ovens or staggered pans if space is limited.
Do not crowd pans or vegetables will steam.
Thighs are forgiving but still need a temperature check.
tonightSpread: Condiments: hot sauce, lemon wedges, ranch
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Chicken thighs in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Pull leftover meat for chicken salad.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Dark meat stays juicy and the vegetables cook in the flavourful pan drippings.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: season chicken overnight and cut vegetables 1 day ahead. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: heat chicken to 165°F.
